approach: Put one guard, `require_origin`, in crates/athena-core/src/gh/remote.rs and call it first in `GitRemote::push`, `replace` and `delete_branch`, so a remote name other than `origin` is refused before any `git push` runs. Add an `ORIGIN` constant, used by landing.rs and early.rs in place of the literal "origin" (imported as `super::remote::ORIGIN`, so mod.rs does not change). Extract the origin lookup in `land_pr` into `landing_target` so the no-origin, local-path and GitHub-origin cases can be tested without a verified job. The scope stays inside the listed deliverables: the records-branch sink (`GitLandingRecords::for_remote`, records.rs) is not changed, and the spec mechanism text states that limit. Tests use temp git repos and a recording `Runner`, with no network. Then fill in OLY-B-BND-01 in docs/spec.toml and add one CHANGELOG line.

decisions.choice: Guard in the shared `GitRemote` write methods (push, replace, delete_branch), failing with an error before `git` is invoked.
decisions.reason: All branch publishing goes through these three methods (`publish_ci_branch` early.rs:352-358, `delete_ci_branch` early.rs:410-412, the `land_pr` remote at landing.rs:887). `GitRemote.name` is a free `&str` (remote.rs:32-35), which is the fault's origin; guarding there covers every present and future caller.

rejected.option: Guard only at the call sites (landing.rs, early.rs)
rejected.why: Leaves the free `name` open to any future caller and guards one path at a time.

rejected.option: Drop the `name` field and hard-code origin
rejected.why: Breaks existing tests and `rebase_job_branch`, which build `GitRemote` with a `remote_name` (landing.rs:770, tests.rs:2700 etc.).
Generic git helpers whose tests push to named remotes; the publishing policy belongs in athena-core.

decisions.choice: Allow exactly the name `origin` (case-sensitive). Anything else, including `""`, `origin2` and `Origin`, is refused.
decisions.reason: `land_pr` and `try_reconcile` hard-code "origin" (landing.rs:865, reconcile.rs:403). An exact match is the smallest rule and prefix tricks cannot get past it.

rejected.option: Compare the remote URL with the project's own GitHub repository
rejected.why: The `origin` of a clone legitimately points anywhere; the boundary is the remote name, and the PR target is parsed from that same remote.

decisions.choice: Do not change records.rs or mod.rs (revision answer to findings 3 and 4). `ORIGIN` is reached from landing.rs/early.rs/tests.rs as `super::remote::ORIGIN`, which works because `mod remote` is a private sibling module (mod.rs:40). The records sink is left as is, and the limit is written in the spec mechanism.
decisions.reason: Both files are outside the listed deliverables and widen the job. Production records sinks are built with the constant origin (landing.rs:887 area passes `remote_name`, which `land_pr` sets to origin; reconcile.rs:403 hard-codes "origin"), so no non-origin path exists today. Guarding `for_remote` is named as a follow-up.

rejected.option: Guard `GitLandingRecords::for_remote` in records.rs and re-export from mod.rs
rejected.why: Outside the deliverables list; the reviewer asked for the smaller scope.

decisions.choice: Extract `landing_target(git, remote_name) -> Result<(String, String)>` from land_pr (landing.rs:865-867): `git remote get-url` then `parse_remote`; `land_pr` calls it with `ORIGIN`.
decisions.reason: The three origin cases then have a direct test. `land_pr` cannot reach that code without a verified job record. Order and error propagation are unchanged.

rejected.option: Test through `Athena::land_pr` with a full verified-job fixture
rejected.why: Needs records, verification and candidate fixtures for a three-line lookup.

decisions.choice: The measure ends `status: not shown` and names the test.
decisions.reason: No `athena status` line reports upstream writes; adding one is out of scope.

rejected.why: Out of scope per the brief.

decisions.choice: Modify CHANGELOG.md with one line under Unreleased/Added.
decisions.reason: It is in the expected deliverables and the changelog default applies, but criterion 7 says it is untouched; this is raised as an open question.

rejected.why: Contradicts the deliverables list and the changelog default.

files.purpose: OLY-B-BND-01: mechanism names crates/athena-core/src/gh/remote.rs `require_origin` (guards GitRemote push, replace, delete_branch; PR calls use the repository parsed from origin via `landing_target`; records-sink pushes are not covered); owner stays Themis; measure names the test and ends `status: not shown`.
Add `ORIGIN` and `require_origin`, and call the guard first in `GitRemote::push`, `replace` and `delete_branch`; update doc comments.
Use `ORIGIN` for `github_repository`, `with_ci_remote` and `early_pr_to`; no change in behavior.
Add the upstream-refusal test, the `landing_target` origin-case tests with a recording Runner, and the no-origin `push_ci_branch` check.
One line under Unreleased/Added for the OLY-B-BND-01 mechanism.

steps: In remote.rs add `pub const ORIGIN: &str = "origin";` and `pub fn require_origin(name: &str, action: &str) -> Result<()>`, which bails unless `name == ORIGIN` with a message such as `refused: {action} to remote {name:?}; Athena publishes only to origin (OLY-B-BND-01)`. Call it as the first statement of `GitRemote::push`, `replace` and `delete_branch`, before any `self.git.run`. Do not change the `Remote` trait or its defaults, or mod.rs.

In landing.rs add `fn landing_target(git: &Git, remote_name: &str) -> Result<(String, String)>`: `git.run(["remote","get-url",remote_name])?` then `parse_remote(&url)`. Replace landing.rs:865-867 with `let remote_name = ORIGIN;` and a call to it, imported as `use super::remote::ORIGIN;`. A missing origin must still error before any `GhClient`, push or record write.
In early.rs replace the literal "origin" strings (github_repository ~:364, with_ci_remote ~:376, early_pr_to ~:460) with `ORIGIN` (`use super::remote::ORIGIN;`).

In tests.rs add `git_remote_refuses_push_replace_and_delete_to_a_non_origin_remote` as described in demonstration 3 (working repo, `origin` and `upstream` bare remotes, seeded upstream branch, refs compared before and after, names `upstream`, `""`, `origin2`, `Origin` refused, `origin` succeeds).
Add a recording `Runner` test struct in tests.rs (arguments recorded, canned JSON, no logic).

In tests.rs add the `landing_target` tests (no origin; local-path origin including the `github.com`-lookalike path; https GitHub origin with `open_pr` argument vectors confined to `repos/example/project/`), and the no-origin `Athena::push_ci_branch` check with the early seam asserting an empty call list.

Edit docs/spec.toml OLY-B-BND-01 (about lines 2396-2402): mechanism = "`require_origin` in crates/athena-core/src/gh/remote.rs refuses push, replace and delete_branch to any remote but origin; PR calls use only the repository parsed from origin (`landing_target`). Records-branch pushes are not covered."; keep owner Themis; measure = "cargo test -p athena-core git_remote_refuses_push_replace_and_delete_to_a_non_origin_remote; status: not shown".
Add the CHANGELOG.md line under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added`.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked`, then `cargo test -p athena-core --test external_calls_guard`, `--test refusal_corpus`, and `cargo test -p xtask --test spec --test policy`. Mutation check: temporarily remove the guard call from `push`, confirm the new test fails, then restore it.

demonstrations.method: Behavior test over real git in temp dirs. Build a working repo with commits c1 and c2, an `origin` bare remote and an `upstream` bare remote with `Git::isolated` and `tempfile`, as at tests.rs:2681-2699. Seed `upstream` with branch `b` at c1 by a direct `git push upstream`, which first shows the push is possible, and record upstream's `for-each-ref`. Call `GitRemote { git, name: "upstream" }`.push, .replace(b, c2, c1) (the pin is correct, so it would succeed unguarded) and .delete_branch(b). Assert each is Err containing `OLY-B-BND-01` and the upstream listing is unchanged. Repeat for names `""`, `origin2` and `Origin`. Then with name `origin` assert push, replace and delete_branch succeed and `remote_head` shows the new commit on origin.
demonstrations.observes: Errors for non-origin names with upstream refs byte-identical; success for origin.
demonstrations.fails_without: With `require_origin` removed from push, replace and delete_branch, the push to `upstream` succeeds, the `unwrap_err` panics, and the upstream refs would differ from the recorded listing.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `GitRemote::push`, `replace`, `delete_branch` (remote.rs:52-79). Fixture: temp repos and bare remotes via `Git::isolated` as in the existing tests at tests.rs:2680-2752; the seam exists and the test only adds the `upstream` remote. No double is used.

demonstrations.method: Three tests. (a) A temp repo with no origin: `landing_target` returns Err, a recording `Runner` has zero calls, and `Athena::push_ci_branch` with the early seam fake (run_pin_tests.rs:582-610 pattern) records no push. (b) Origin is a local path: `landing_target` returns Err (`only github.com remotes are supported`, client.rs:1200), `GhClient::origin_repository` returns None, and the recording Runner has zero calls. A path containing `github.com` is checked in the same test; it records today's `parse_remote` substring behavior (client.rs:1199) and is noted as a risk. (c) Origin is `https://github.com/example/project.git`: `landing_target` returns (github.com, example/project). A `GhClient::new(&runner, repo)` built from it calls `open_pr`, and every recorded gh argument vector targets `repos/example/project/` and no other repository. A `GitRemote` named origin pushes only to the bare repository origin points at, while a bare `upstream` stays unchanged.
demonstrations.observes: Err and zero writes with no origin; Err and zero gh calls with a local path; (github.com, example/project) and gh calls confined to that repository for the https origin.
demonstrations.fails_without: If `landing_target` accepted a local-path origin, or the client were built for a repository other than the one parsed from origin, the Err assertion or the repository-confinement assertion would fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `landing_target` (extracted from `Athena::land_pr`, landing.rs:865-867; added by plan step 3), `GhClient::origin_repository` (client.rs:1026, exists), `Athena::push_ci_branch` (early.rs:384, exists) with `early_seam::install` (gh/mod.rs:99, exists). Fixtures: temp repos with `git remote add origin <url>`; a new recording `Runner` test struct in tests.rs (trait at transport.rs:13, modelled on `ScriptRunner` at tests.rs:4794) added by plan step 6. It only records argument vectors and returns canned JSON, with no origin or parse logic.
